instrument: Royce 1899 Schedule (as crosswalked)
summary: The crosswalk has 1,172 role rows over 724 Royce area ids. Distinct areas per role: reserved 469, confirmed 51, described_or_recognized 36, retroceded 57, us_reserved 4, ceded 402, ceded_part 16, other 62. 498 areas carry at least one promise role (reserved/confirmed/described_or_recognized).
federal_account_contrast: Royce already records promised land; the atlas's 'ceded' framing hides that two-thirds of polygons began as land reserved or recognized to a nation.
map_implication: Add a 'promised' layer filter built from roles reserved/confirmed/described_or_recognized; no new geometry needed for 491 of 498 areas.
notes: Counts are distinct area ids; one area can hold several roles. Role labels are the crosswalk's, assigned by an earlier pipeline from Royce remarks.

source_doc: treaty-land-atlas repo: crosswalks/royce-entry-roles.csv + data/derived/cessions.json (computed by research agent)
instrument: Royce 1899 Schedule (as crosswalked)
summary: Of 498 promised areas: 259 ended ceded or taken by Royce's last date (256 with geometry, about 370 million acres summed), 227 were still 'kept' (226 with geometry, about 359 million acres summed), 12 unclear (about 23 million acres). Seven areas have no geometry (Royce 47, 65, 128, 129, 130, 543, 690); 690 (Meskwaki, Tama County) is a promise-role area without geometry.
federal_account_contrast: Acre sums overlap (Royce polygons stack, e.g. 1851 territories under later reserves), so they show scale, not a land balance.
map_implication: Show 'promised then lost' (status ceded/taken with a promise role) as its own class distinct from plain cessions; never sum overlapping acres in UI copy.
notes: Areas computed by spherical-excess formula on the repo GeoJSON; overlapping polygons double-count. 'Kept' means kept as of Royce's input dates (to 1894), not today.

source_doc: treaty-land-atlas repo: crosswalks/royce-entry-roles.csv + data/derived/cessions.json (computed by research agent); src/lib/land.ts ROLE_KIND
instrument: General Allotment Act Feb. 8, 1887 and surplus-land acts
summary: Royce ends in 1894, so 'kept' freezes reservations before most allotment and surplus-land openings. Indian landholding fell from about 138 million acres (1887) to about 48 million (1934). Royce 700-705 (Sioux), 715 (Crow), 374 (Flathead), 540 (Wind River) are all shown kept but were opened after 1900.
sources_cited_by_source: FEMA EMI IS-650b allotment page; Encyclopedia of the Great Plains
federal_account_contrast: The map's 'kept' green overstates what nations held in the 20th century; diminishment came by statute, not treaty.
map_implication: Rename 'kept' to 'still reserved in 1894' and add a post-1894 overlay (opening acts) before claiming land is still Native-held.
notes: 138M/48M figures repeated by many secondary sources; some cite ~100M lost. Use 'about 90 million acres'.

place: Fort Laramie / Horse Creek, Nebraska Territory (approx. 41.95N, -103.95W treaty ground at Horse Creek)
instrument: Treaty of Fort Laramie, Sept. 17, 1851
summary: Article 5 defines by metes and bounds the territory of each nation; the nations did not abandon claims to other lands. The repo maps these as 'described_or_recognized' but only in fragments: there is no single polygon per nation, and area 300 is labelled 'several nations' at only 6.3 million acres.
verbatim_quote: the aforesaid Indian nations do not hereby abandon or prejudice any rights or claims they may have to other lands
federal_account_contrast: The treaty recognized (did not grant) Native title; it was not a cession at all.
map_implication: Digitize all seven Art. 5 territories as named 'recognized 1851' polygons (descriptions in web-promised.md) and draw them as promised land beneath later cessions.
notes: Quote taken from widely reprinted Kappler text; verify exact wording against Kappler page image. Stat. cite uncertain because the treaty was never proclaimed.

nations: Sioux; Cheyenne; Arapaho; Crow; Assiniboine; Gros Ventre; Mandan; Arikara
instrument: Senate amendment to Fort Laramie Treaty 1851
summary: The Senate cut annuities from 50 years to 10 (plus 5 at the President's discretion). Assent was sought from the nations; sources say all but the Crow assented. The treaty was never proclaimed, but Court of Claims cases later treated it as valid. The repo repeats Royce's line that it was 'never ratified'.
federal_account_contrast: Royce's 'never ratified' wording, copied into crosswalk summaries for 426, 517, 398, 399, makes the 1851 promise look void, when the Senate consented with an amendment.
map_implication: Correct crosswalk summaries: 'ratified by Senate with amendment 1852, never proclaimed'; tag 1851 areas SENATE_AMENDED_NO_CONSENT for the Crow.
notes: Single government source for May 24, 1852 date per search summary; verify against Senate Executive Journal.

source_doc: Fort Laramie Treaty 1868 Art. 11, 16; treaty-land-atlas repo: crosswalks/royce-entry-roles.csv + data/derived/cessions.json (computed by research agent)
place: north of North Platte, east of Big Horn summits (Wyoming, Montana, Nebraska)
instrument: Fort Laramie 1868 Art. 16; Sioux agreement June 23, 1875; agreement Sept. 26, 1876 / act Feb. 28, 1877
summary: Art. 16 kept the country north of the North Platte and east of the Big Horn summits as 'unceded Indian territory' closed to whites; Art. 11 kept hunting on the Republican Fork. These were extinguished by the 1875 agreement (584) and the 1876-77 Black Hills agreement/act (597).
verbatim_quote: shall be held and considered to be unceded Indian territory
federal_account_contrast: Repo shows 597 'ceded' by the 1876 agreement, though that agreement lacked the Art. 12 three-fourths signatures.
map_implication: Mark 597 as 'unceded territory taken by 1877 act without Art. 12 consent'.
notes: Statute cite 19 Stat. 254 from general knowledge; verify.

source_doc: United States v. Sioux Nation of Indians, 448 U.S. 371 (1980); Encyclopedia of the Great Plains (egp.law.050); NARF bulletin Different Horse v. Salazar
instrument: Act of Feb. 28, 1877
summary: The 1877 act took the Black Hills without the three-fourths adult male consent Art. 12 required. The Supreme Court held it a taking and affirmed about $17.1 million plus interest (about $106 million). The Sioux refuse the money; the fund has grown to an estimated $1-2 billion.
federal_account_contrast: Royce and the repo list 598 as a 'cession'. The Court found compensation owed; it did not return land.
map_implication: Flag Royce 598 'taken without Art. 12 consent; payment refused'. Link ICC Dkt 74-B.
notes: Fund size varies by source (~$650M late 2000s; ~$2B recent); avoid one precise figure.

source_doc: treaty-land-atlas repo: crosswalks/royce-entry-roles.csv + data/derived/cessions.json (computed by research agent); Lone Wolf v. Hitchcock, 187 U.S. 553 (1903); Kansapedia; Supreme Court Historical Society
instrument: Little Arkansas treaty Oct. 18, 1865; Medicine Lodge Oct. 21, 1867 Art. 2, 12; Jerome Agreement 1892 ratified act June 6, 1900
summary: The 1865 reserve (511, about 43 million acres in repo polygon, incl. Texas Panhandle) was cut in 1867 to the Medicine Lodge reservation between the Washita and Red rivers. Art. 12 required three-fourths of adult men to sign any cession. The 1892 Jerome Agreement lacked that; Congress ratified it in 1900, taking about 2.99 million acres, and Lone Wolf upheld Congress's power to abrogate.
verbatim_quote: signed by at least three-fourths of all the adult male Indians occupying the same
sources_cited_by_source: Medicine Lodge Art. 12 (quoted in 187 U.S. 553 syllabus)
federal_account_contrast: Royce's last date for 478 'kept' predates the 1900-01 opening; the map shows it intact.
map_implication: Add 1901 opening of KCA surplus lands as a post-Royce taking over Royce 478.
notes: Signatures alleged counterfeit (SCHS); treat as contested.

instrument: Medicine Lodge (Cheyenne-Arapaho) Oct. 28, 1867; EO Aug. 10, 1869; act Mar. 3, 1891
royce_areas: 525 (1869 reserve); 1867 treaty reserve not found as its own repo area
summary: The 1867 treaty reservation lay in the Cherokee Outlet; the nations never settled there and an 1869 executive order substituted a reserve on the North Canadian and Washita (525, 4.3 million acres), which was ceded subject to allotment in 1891.
federal_account_contrast: The treaty-promised reserve vanishes from the map because Royce folds it into Cherokee Outlet area 489.
map_implication: Digitize the 1867 Art. 2 reserve as promised-never-delivered, overlapping 489.
notes: Royce number for the 1867 reserve not confirmed in repo; check Royce Indian Territory plate.

source_doc: treaty-land-atlas repo: crosswalks/royce-entry-roles.csv + data/derived/cessions.json (computed by research agent); accessgenealogy; military-history wiki (Little Arkansas)

summary: Fort Wise ceded most of the 1851 territory (426, about 47 million acres in repo polygon) and reserved a tract on the Arkansas and Sand Creek (477, 3.7 million acres). The Sand Creek massacre happened in that area in 1864; the 1865 treaty then ceded the reserve and promised a new one partly in Kansas, which was never set up.
verbatim_quote: no part of which should be within the state of Kansas
federal_account_contrast: Repo shows 477 as 'ceded' in 1865, just 11 months after the massacre on that land.
map_implication: Flag 477 'reserve where the Sand Creek massacre occurred, ceded 1865'; show 1865 Art. 2 reserve as promised, never established.
notes: Quote is a paraphrase-quote in a secondary source, not the treaty text; verify. Sand Creek NHS coords approximate.

source_doc: Ute Treaty Mar. 2, 1868 (Kappler 2:990); treaty-land-atlas repo: crosswalks/royce-entry-roles.csv + data/derived/cessions.json (computed by research agent); Univ. of Utah collections (act June 15, 1880); Aspen Journalism

summary: Art. 2 reserved Colorado west of the 107th meridian and south of a line 15 miles north of the 40th parallel (566+616+617, about 16 million acres in repo polygons). Brunot (1873) took the San Juan strip (566); after the 1879 Meeker events the 1880 act removed White River and Uncompahgre Utes, leaving the Southern Ute strip (617).
federal_account_contrast: Repo notes it is unsure which of 616/617 is ceded vs retained.
map_implication: Draw the 1868 Art. 2 rectangle as one promised polygon; resolve 616/617 from Royce Colorado plate.
notes: Stat. cites for 1874/1880 from general knowledge; verify.

source_doc: WyoHistory.org 'Coming to Wind River'; treaty-land-atlas repo: crosswalks/royce-entry-roles.csv + data/derived/cessions.json (computed by research agent); Wyoming v. EPA, 875 F.3d 505 (10th Cir. 2017), cert. denied 138 S. Ct. 2677 (2018)
instrument: Fort Bridger 1863; Fort Bridger July 3, 1868 Art. 2; Brunot/Lander cession 1872 (act 1874); act Mar. 3, 1905
summary: The 1863 treaty recognized about 44 million acres of Shoshone country; the 1868 treaty reserved about 3 million (539+540 = 3.2 million acres in repo). The southern part was ceded in 1872 (539). The 1905 act opened land north of the Big Wind River; in 2017 the Tenth Circuit held that act diminished the reservation (Riverton outside).
verbatim_quote: Congress evinced a clear intent to diminish the Reservation
federal_account_contrast: Repo status for 540 is 'unclear' and stops in 1894; 20th-century diminishment absent.
map_implication: Add Wyoming v. EPA as a diminishment overlay on 540; contrast with McGirt.
notes: 1863 Stat. cite and 1905 cite from general knowledge; verify. Quote from search-result summary of the opinion.

source_doc: Andrew Jackson, Letter to the Creek Indians, Mar. 23, 1829 (American Presidency Project); Papers of Andrew Jackson (UTK), Jackson to David W. Haley, Oct. 15, 1829
instrument: Presidential talk (not a treaty)
summary: Jackson told the Creeks the western land would be theirs 'as long as the grass grows or the water runs'. This is a presidential promise, not treaty text; the binding guarantees are in the Removal Act sec. 3 and the removal treaties.
verbatim_quote: as long as the grass grows or the water runs, in peace and plenty
federal_account_contrast: Often misattributed to a treaty; the map should cite it as a talk.
map_implication: Use in narrative captions for Indian Territory, attributed to Jackson's 1829 letter, not to a treaty.
notes: Wording varies slightly between the March letter and the Oct. draft.

source_doc: McGirt v. Oklahoma, 591 U.S. 894 (2020) slip op.; 221 U.S. 286; 1890 CIA report via accessgenealogy; treaty-land-atlas repo: crosswalks/royce-entry-roles.csv + data/derived/cessions.json (computed by research agent)
place: Indian Territory between the Arkansas and Canadian rivers
instrument: Creek Treaty Mar. 24, 1832 Art. XIV; Creek Treaty Feb. 14, 1833; Creek patent Aug. 11, 1852; Creek Treaty 1866; Creek agreement 1889
summary: The 1832 and 1833 treaties promised the Creeks a 'permanent home' with a fee patent (issued 1852). The 1866 treaty took the western half (486/698); allotment followed. McGirt held the 1866 reservation was never disestablished.
verbatim_quote: permanent home to the whole Creek Nation of Indians
federal_account_contrast: The repo marks the Creek eastern domain via Royce as reserved and the today layer (Census) shows only 'Creek OTSA (statistical)'.
map_implication: Show the Muscogee Reservation (1866 boundaries) as a legal reservation today, citing McGirt, and relabel the Census OTSA.
notes: Sources disagree whether fee promise is in 1833 or 1834 instrument.

source_doc: 1890 Commissioner of Indian Affairs report via accessgenealogy; Treaty of New Echota 1835 Art. 5; treaty-land-atlas repo: crosswalks/royce-entry-roles.csv + data/derived/cessions.json (computed by research agent)
place: Cherokee Nation, Indian Territory; Cherokee Outlet; Cherokee Neutral Land (Kansas)
instrument: Cherokee Treaty 1828; 1833; New Echota 1835 Art. 2, 5; patent Dec. 31, 1838; 1866 treaty; Cherokee Outlet agreement (act Mar. 3, 1893)
summary: New Echota (signed by the minority Ridge faction) confirmed 7 million acres plus a 'perpetual outlet' west and promised no state jurisdiction without consent. The Neutral Land (490) was put in trust for sale in 1866; the Outlet (489, about 8 million acres in repo) was sold in 1893; the remaining Cherokee Nation (492) was allotted and absorbed into Oklahoma in 1907.
verbatim_quote: the lands hereby granted shall revert to the United States if the said Cherokees become extinct or abandon the same
sources_cited_by_source: 1838 patent text quoted in 1890 CIA report
federal_account_contrast: Repo status for 492 is 'kept' (Royce era); allotment and statehood, which broke the 'no state' clause, are absent.
map_implication: Mark 492 kept-in-1894 then allotted; flag 489 and 490 as promised then sold; post-McGirt state court ruling (Hogner 2021) says the reservation persists.
notes: Hogner v. State (Okla. Crim. App. 2021) from general knowledge; verify. Stat. cites for 1893 act unverified.

source_doc: 1890 CIA report via accessgenealogy; treaty-land-atlas repo: crosswalks/royce-entry-roles.csv + data/derived/cessions.json (computed by research agent)
place: Indian Territory south of the Canadian
instrument: Dancing Rabbit Creek 1830; Choctaw patent Mar. 23, 1842; Choctaw-Chickasaw treaty 1855; treaty 1866 (Leased District)
summary: The 1842 patent gave the Choctaw (with Chickasaw lands) a fee title. The 1855 treaty 'leased' the land west of 98 degrees; the 1866 treaty ceded that Leased District (485) for $300,000, which went largely to the Kiowa-Comanche and Wichita reservations.
verbatim_quote: in fee simple to them and their descendants
federal_account_contrast: Repo marks 368 status unclear; Royce dates the cession to 1866.
map_implication: Show 367 as patented promised land; 485 'leased then ceded'.
notes: Choctaw and Chickasaw reservation persistence affirmed by Okla. Crim. App. in 2021 (Sizemore; Bosse) per general knowledge; verify.

place: Ohio/Indiana; line from Cuyahoga River via Fort Laurens and Loramie's to Fort Recovery and the Ohio opposite the Kentucky River
instrument: Treaty of Greenville, Art. 3-5
summary: Art. 4 relinquished US claims to Indian lands north and west of the Greenville line, and Art. 5 says the tribes 'are quietly to enjoy them'. That promised zone has no polygon of its own in the repo; it appears only as later cessions (1803-1840s).
verbatim_quote: the Indian tribes who have a right to those lands, are quietly to enjoy them
federal_account_contrast: The map shows only ceded land south/east of the line, not the guaranteed land beyond it.
map_implication: Draw the Greenville line as a 'promised boundary' and shade land beyond it 1795-1805 as guaranteed Native land.
notes: Quote from widely reprinted Art. 5 text; verify.

source_doc: Wikipedia 'Hellgate Treaty'; Montana Historical Society Charlo biography; Char-Koosta News; treaty-land-atlas repo: crosswalks/royce-entry-roles.csv + data/derived/cessions.json (computed by research agent)
place: Bitterroot Valley and Jocko (Flathead) Valley, Montana
instrument: Hellgate Treaty July 16, 1855 Art. 2, 11; EO Nov. 14, 1871; Garfield agreement 1872; Flathead Allotment Act Apr. 23, 1904
summary: Art. 11 promised a survey of the Bitterroot Valley before deciding the Salish reservation; the survey was not done before an 1871 order directed removal. Charlo's mark on the 1872 Garfield agreement is described by the Montana Historical Society as not signed by him. Troops moved the band in 1891. The Jocko reservation (374, 1.46 million acres in repo) was opened by the 1904 act.
verbatim_quote: Charlo never signed the document
federal_account_contrast: Repo has 374 'kept' and no polygon for the conditional Bitterroot reserve.
map_implication: Draw Bitterroot Valley above Lolo Fork as 'conditionally promised 1855, taken 1871-91'; add 1904/1910 opening over 374.
notes: Quote is search-summary paraphrase; get exact MHS wording. 1904 cite from general knowledge.

source_doc: treaty-land-atlas repo: crosswalks/royce-entry-roles.csv + data/derived/cessions.json (computed by research agent)
instrument: Nez Perce Treaty 1855; Treaty 1863; agreement 1893 (act Aug. 15, 1894)
summary: The 1855 reserve (441, about 6.6 million acres in repo) was cut in 1863 to about 770,000 acres (442), signed by bands whose own lands lay inside the reduced reserve; non-treaty bands (Joseph's Wallowa) never signed. Unallotted 442 land was ceded in 1893.
federal_account_contrast: Royce records a cession by 'the Nez Perce' as one body.
map_implication: Flag 441 cession 'by treaty bands only; non-treaty bands did not consent'.

source_doc: Navajo Treaty June 1, 1868 Art. 2 (Kappler 2:1015); treaty-land-atlas repo: crosswalks/royce-entry-roles.csv + data/derived/cessions.json (computed by research agent)
place: Arizona/New Mexico; Bosque Redondo (Fort Sumner, NM) signing
instrument: Treaty of Bosque Redondo, June 1, 1868
summary: Signed while the Dine were held at Bosque Redondo after the Long Walk. Art. 2 reserved land bounded by 37N, a line through old Fort Defiance, a meridian through Bear Spring, and about 109 30'W (518, 3.3 million acres in repo). One of few promised reservations later enlarged (608, 615 and many 20th-century additions).
federal_account_contrast: Royce 519 'relinquishment' was signed in confinement.

source_doc: treaty-land-atlas repo: crosswalks/royce-entry-roles.csv + data/derived/cessions.json (computed by research agent); Heizer 1972 (via search); Wikipedia 'California Indian Reservations and Cessions'; Mechoopda tribal site
instrument: 18 unratified California treaties (Barbour, McKee, Wozencraft)
summary: The repo has 19 reserve polygons from the 18 treaties, summing to about 8.5 million acres (sources give 7.4-8.5 million). All are status 'kept', but the Senate rejected the treaties and filed them under secrecy until 1905, so the reserves never existed in law.
verbatim_quote: Reservation set apart by the unratified treaty of Apr. 29, 1851, not a cession.
federal_account_contrast: 'Kept' wrongly implies Native nations held these lands; in fact they were promised and never delivered, and the matching 'ceded' areas (274, 279 etc.) were never ceded either.
map_implication: New status 'promised, never delivered' for the 19 CA reserves; status 'taken without ratified cession' for their paired cession areas.
notes: Acreage is repo-polygon sum and overlaps nothing else in CA as far as checked.

source_doc: treaty-land-atlas repo: crosswalks/royce-entry-roles.csv + data/derived/cessions.json (computed by research agent)
nations: Delaware; Shawnee; Potawatomi; Sauk and Fox; Kickapoo; Chippewa and Munsee; Ottawa; Miami; Wyandot; Kaw; Iowa
instrument: Removal-era treaties 1825-1846; Kansas reductions 1854-1867
summary: Nations removed to Kansas were promised permanent homes there, then the 1854 Kansas-Nebraska opening led to a chain of reductions, trust sales and railroad sales (e.g. Delaware remainder sold to a railroad, 488) and a second removal to Indian Territory by 1867-1873.
verbatim_quote: the remainder sold to the Missouri River Railroad Company
federal_account_contrast: Royce codes most as 'ceded' or 'sold in trust', hiding that they were the promised permanent homes of removal.
map_implication: Tag Kansas reserves as 'second promise' (post-removal) and link each to its removal treaty.
notes: Stat. cites from general knowledge.

source_doc: McGirt v. Oklahoma (2020) via teachingamericanhistory.org, Indianz, Osage News
place: eastern Oklahoma (about 3 million acres incl. most of Tulsa)
instrument: McGirt v. Oklahoma
summary: 5-4, Gorsuch: only Congress can disestablish a reservation, and it must say so clearly; allotment, statehood and loss of tribal government did not do it. The Creek reservation remains Indian country for federal criminal law.
verbatim_quote: Because Congress has not said otherwise, we hold the government to its word.
federal_account_contrast: Shows a treaty promise can survive allotment in law, so 'promised' is not only history.
map_implication: Model McGirt as the template for 'promised and still legally reservation'; label Census OTSA layer accordingly.
notes: Oklahoma v. Castro-Huerta (2022) later allowed state jurisdiction over non-Indian defendants; mention in caption.

source_doc: Solem v. Bartlett 465 U.S. 463 (1984); Nebraska v. Parker 577 U.S. 481 (2016); South Dakota v. Yankton Sioux 522 U.S. 329 (1998); Hagen v. Utah 510 U.S. 399 (1994); Rosebud Sioux v. Kneip 430 U.S. 584 (1977)
nations: Cheyenne River Sioux; Omaha; Yankton Sioux; Ute (Uintah); Rosebud Sioux
instrument: Surplus-land acts 1892-1910
summary: Courts split on whether surplus-land acts shrank reservations: not diminished (Solem, Cheyenne River 1908 act; Parker, Omaha 1882 act); diminished (Rosebud 1904-1910 acts; Yankton 1894 act; Hagen, Uintah 1902-05 acts; Wind River 1905 per 10th Cir.).
federal_account_contrast: Royce cannot show any of this; boundaries today depend on case law, not on the 1894 map.
map_implication: Build a 'diminishment status' attribute per reservation (not diminished / diminished / disputed) with the controlling case.
notes: Case holdings from general legal knowledge, not fetched this pass; verify each before publishing.

source_doc: USGS pubs 70114965; USGS Store product 101505; LOC item 80695449; UND Commons indigenous-gov-docs/168; NILL ICC final report
instrument: Indian Land Areas Judicially Established (map, 1:4,000,000, Albers)
summary: USGS map prepared for the ICC final report showing areas where a tribe proved aboriginal occupancy before the ICC or Court of Claims. Print $9 from USGS; scans at LOC and UND. Federal work, so public domain.
federal_account_contrast: Shows 'judicially established' original title, the closest federal map to Native land as such rather than cession.
map_implication: Use as a source for 'land recognized by ICC but paid for, not returned'; georeference LOC scan if vector copies are unusable.
notes: Pages not fetched (DNS blocked); facts from search-result abstracts.

source_doc: ArcGIS services1.arcgis.com .../Indian_Land_Areas_Judicially_Established_1978/FeatureServer; gis.cdatribe-nsn.gov .../Boundaries_JudiciallyEstablishedIndianLands
instrument: Vector versions of the 1978 ICC map
summary: Two vector copies exist: an Esri-hosted FeatureServer (layer 5, polygons, GeoJSON query, max 2,000 records, shown with 2016 BIA tribal boundaries) and a Coeur d'Alene Tribe GIS service with fields TRIBAL_OWNER, DOCKET, DATE_EXISTED, CITATIONS, TRIBE (EPSG 26911). The tribal service warns it is not a legal boundary.
verbatim_quote: should NOT be considered "gospel"
map_implication: Best candidate geometry for an ICC layer; DOCKET field enables links to ICC decisions. Confirm license/permission with owners (Esri item owner unknown; CDA Tribe).
notes: Hosts blocked from this sandbox; metadata from search snippets only. License not confirmed.

source_doc: Native Land Digital treaty page 'treaty-of-fort-laramie-1851-1868'; USFS PDF '1851 Fort Laramie Treaty of Common References'; ospi.k12.wa.us/UM Regional Learning Project map; repo docs/data/E1
instrument: Fort Laramie 1851 GIS sources
summary: No openly licensed vector layer of the seven 1851 territories was found. NLD has a combined 1851/1868 polygon (updated June 2022) but its terms bar storing/distributing API data without permission (repo E1). The USFS PDF is treaty text; the UM map is a PDF image.
map_implication: Digitize Art. 5 descriptions in-house onto rivers (NHD) and ranges, citing Kappler; use Royce polygons as a check. Do not ingest NLD geometry.
notes: Absence of an open dataset is a search result, not proof.

source_doc: repo seed-data/geodata-sources.csv GEO-004, GEO-010, GEO-011, GEO-017..020
instrument: Present-day and parcel datasets already in inventory
summary: Census AIANNH (public domain, statistical), BIA LAR (reference only), Land-Grab U (license conflict CC0 vs ODbL/CC BY-SA), NLD (restricted). None gives historical promised boundaries, but AIANNH/LAR vs Royce 'reserved' gives a 'promised then vs held now' comparison.
map_implication: Compute per-nation 'promised (Royce reserved/recognized, earliest) vs today (AIANNH)' ratios, with overlap caveats.
